skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

6. // `Result::and_then`: on `Ok`, the closure is applied to the payload (its precondition must hold);
7. // on `Err`, the error is forwarded unchanged. Mirrors `core`'s implementation. vstd ships no
8. // specification for it.
9. pub assume_specification<T, E, U, F: FnOnce(T) -> Result<U, E>>[ Result::<T, E>::and_then ](
10.     result: Result<T, E>,
11.     op: F,
12. ) -> (res: Result<U, E>)
13.     requires
14.         result is Ok ==> op.requires((result->Ok_0,)),
15.     ensures
16.         result is Err ==> res == Err::<U, E>(result->Err_0),
17.         result is Ok ==> op.ensures((result->Ok_0,), res),
18. ;
19. 
20. // `Result::inspect_err`: runs a side-effecting closure on the error (if any) and returns the
21. // receiver unchanged. The closure is used purely for its effects, so no abstract obligation is
22. // threaded. vstd ships no specification for it.
23. pub assume_specification<T, E, F: FnOnce(&E)>[ Result::<T, E>::inspect_err ](
24.     result: Result<T, E>,
25.     f: F,
26. ) -> (res: Result<T, E>)
27.     ensures
28.         res == result,
29. ;
30.

32. // ships no specification for it.
33. pub assume_specification<T, A: ::core::alloc::Allocator>[ Vec::<T, A>::capacity ](
34.     vec: &Vec<T, A>,
35. ) -> (c: usize)
36. ;

42. /// The kernel watermark: the number of physical frames the kernel always keeps free for itself.
43. ///
44. /// User allocations are gated by this threshold; kernel allocations bypass it. Mirrors the
45. /// build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`, which is generated by the `config`
46. /// crate's `build.rs` (from `kernel_config.toml`) and therefore lives outside Verus's view.
47. /// The abstract value is fixed by the `external_body` accessor `kernel_watermark()`; this is an
48. /// external-bottom trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). Callers do not depend on
49. /// the concrete threshold — only on the fact that user allocations are gated by it.
50. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> nat;
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Allocation / watermark vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl FrameAllocView {
57.     /// Number of frames currently free, i.e. available to hand out. This is the single quantity
58.     /// the kernel watermark reads. Models `frame::free_count()`.
59.     pub open spec fn free_count(self) -> nat {
60.         self.free_frames.len()
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible: fulfilling it would still leave at
64.     /// least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames free for the kernel. This is the predicate behind the
65.     /// user-vs-kernel asymmetry that `check_user_watermark` enforces.
66.     pub open spec fn user_alloc_ok(self, count: nat) -> bool {
67.         self.free_count() >= count + spec_kernel_watermark()
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Allocate a single currently-free frame `addr`: move it from `free_frames` to
71.     /// `allocated_frames` with refcount 1. (Equivalent to `book_all(set![addr])`.)
72.     pub open spec fn alloc_one(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
73.         FrameAllocView {
74.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
75.             free_frames: self.free_frames.remove(addr),
76.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
77.         }
78.     }
79. }

91.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView {

98.     /// disjoint, page-aligned, refcount <-> allocated consistent, refcounts in 1..=255).
99.     ///
100.     /// Liveness is structural (a `&mut self` is only obtainable after `init` succeeded) and the
101.     /// watermark is a per-user-allocation gate, not an invariant — kernel allocations are
102.     /// designed to dip below it — so neither appears here.
103.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
104.         self@.wf()
105.     }
106. }
107. 
108. //==================================================================================================

112. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of user-frame handles.
113. pub open spec fn user_addr_set(frames: Seq<UserFrame>) -> Set<int> {

124. /// identity-map contiguity guarantee that kernel-stack callers (`alloc_kpages`) depend on.

---
name: proving-guide
description: "Proving methodology and mindset for Verus verification: function-by-function approach, persistence through failures, clean verification, and bug reporting. Use when writing proofs or resolving verification failures."
---

# Proving Guide

Read `verus-constraints` first. See `verus-syntax` for attribute-based syntax
reference. Study `docs/examples/binary-search/proof/` for a working example.

## Core Approach

1. **One function at a time.** Resolve `admit()` function by function,
   following the order from the `verification-order` skill if a
   verification plan exists. Do not move to the next function until the
   current one verifies cleanly.
   
   The current module's functions must NOT have `external_body`.
   Do NOT add `external_body` to any function during proving.

2. **Keep trying.** When verification fails, read the error log carefully,
   try a different proof strategy, and iterate. You are capable of solving
   this — if one approach fails, try the next. Do not give up or ask for
   suggestions; work through possible approaches systematically.

3. **Never weaken specs.** If a spec is hard to prove, the proof strategy
   is wrong — not the spec. Do not relax `requires`, weaken `ensures`,
   or remove clauses to make proofs easier. The spec is the contract.

4. **Report genuine bugs.** If after thorough attempts you determine the
   failure is caused by a code bug (not a proof gap), report it immediately
   using the `bug-reporting` skill. Do not silently work around code bugs.

5. **Clean verification.** After all proofs pass, check for warnings and
   resolve them. A clean verification has zero errors AND zero warnings.
   Trigger warnings are especially common and must not be left: add
   explicit `#[trigger]` annotations or restructure quantifiers until
   all trigger warnings are gone.

## Verification Tool

Use `make verify-<crate> MODULE=<module>` to verify the current module during
proving. After all modules are done, run `make verify-<crate>` (no MODULE) to
confirm the full crate still passes. The output includes:
- **Verification result** — pass/fail with error details
- **Cheating detection** — flags `admit`, `assume`, `external_body`, `trusted`,
  cfg-gated exec code; all must be resolved in current module.
  `external_body` on direct callees in dependency modules is expected
  until those modules are verified; **Never** mark callers
  (upstream modules) as `external_body`
- **Coverage** — which functions have contracts

After verification passes, use the `ast-consistency` skill to check that
exec code was not accidentally modified during proving. Fix all
inconsistencies before finalizing.

---

## Proof Organization

- **Write proof helpers in `.proof.rs` from the start.** If a proof block
  would exceed ~5 lines, don't write it inline — define a `proof fn` in the
  `.proof.rs` file and call it from the inline `proof { }` block. Same for
  loop invariants with more than ~5 clauses: define a `spec fn` predicate in
  `.proof.rs` and reference it in the `invariant` clause. This avoids
  cluttering exec code and eliminates extraction work later.
- Keep proof fn granular: one lemma per function, chain via `assert ... by { lemma_call(); }`
- Default: make specs `opaque`, only `reveal()` where needed

## Inductive Invariants

Functions with loops or recursion need inductive invariants — without them
Verus cannot verify the function. If loop invariants already exist, review
them before attempting the proof. When `admit()` is removed, existing
invariants may turn out to be too weak. Strengthen them — do not work
around the failure with cheating. If no invariant exists yet, define one
before attempting the proof.

1. **Review the existing invariant.** Read the `invariant` clause (or the
   `spec fn` it references). Understand what it claims and what it misses.
2. **Strengthen as needed.** Add missing clauses or tighten existing ones
   based on Verus error messages. Getting the invariant right on the first
   try is rare — iterate until it passes. Never bypass a failing obligation
   with `admit`, `assume`, or `external_body`.
3. **Verify the three obligations:**
   - **Base case** — the invariant holds on entry (before the first
     iteration, or for the base constructor).
   - **Inductive step** — if the invariant holds before an iteration /
     recursive call, it holds after.
   - **Sufficiency** — the invariant, combined with the loop exit
     condition, implies the postcondition.

# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
  `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
  entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
  `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
  so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
  This matches the inherited upstream
  `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
  `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
  `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

## Skip / exclude from current proof target

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::phys`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates an
  `alloc::collections::LinkedList` in a `for` loop. Verus has no `LinkedList` model and the
  orphan rule blocks providing one from the kernel crate (see
  `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,
  every frame in `phys_regions_frame_set(&physical_memory_regions)` becomes reserved.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same `LinkedList` limitation.
  `ensures` states that, on `Ok`, every *covered* frame in `mmio_regions_frame_set(mmio_regions)`
  becomes reserved (uncovered MMIO frames are skipped, matching the `frame::is_covered` gate).

## Cross-module dependencies marked `external_body` (eliminated when their module is verified)

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init` — also listed under skip; callable from verified `init`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::init` — no specs yet; opaque callee.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::Upool` (struct) and `Upool::new` — no specs yet; opaque
  type/callee needed so verified `init` can construct the user page pool.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::Upool::alloc` — pool allocation primitive the manager's user
  paths call. `ensures` describes the free→allocated transition (`alloc_one`) and the empty-pool
  `Err` arm (`free_count() == 0`). Verified when `upool` is.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::new` — wraps a `FrameAddress` into an owning
  kernel-frame handle. `ensures Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@`. Verified when `kframe` is.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc`;
  `ensures Ok(frame) => frame.inv()`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc_contiguous` — singleton wrapper around
  `Inner::alloc_contiguous`; `requires count > 0`, `ensures` page-aligned base plus the
  address-space range bound the manager's index arithmetic relies upon.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::free_count` — reports the free-partition size
  (`== phys_view().frames.free_count()`).
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::free` — best-effort frame release used by manager error
  cleanup; no precondition, no abstract postcondition (callers ignore the outcome).
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::book` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::book`. Reserves a
  covered, previously-free frame so `alloc` never hands it out. `requires phys_addr.inv()`,
  `ensures Ok(()) => phys_view().frames.reserved(phys_addr@)`. The free→allocated transition
  lives in `Inner::book` (verified in-body); the wrapper's postcondition references the
  *post-mutation* `phys_view().frames`, which the parameter-free `phys_view()` accessor cannot
  express until the §8 ghost token is realized (`instance()` pins it to the *pre*-state). Same
  cross-module deferral as `frame::alloc`; `external_body` until the free-function layer is
  verified.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc_range` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc_range`.
  On success every (free) frame in the region is reserved. `requires region.inv()`,
  `ensures Ok(()) => phys_view().frames.all_reserved(region_frame_addrs(..))`. Same
  post-mutation `phys_view()` deferral as `frame::book`; `external_body` until the free-function
  layer is verified.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::share` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::share` (the CoW

## Observations (record-only; validated in the proving phase)

### OBS-1: `alloc_many_kernel_frames` lacks the `count == 0` fast-path guard

`alloc_many_user_frames` early-returns `Ok(())` when `count == 0`, but
`alloc_many_kernel_frames` has no such guard and unconditionally calls
`frame::alloc_contiguous(count)`. `Inner::alloc_contiguous` (and therefore the
`frame::alloc_contiguous` wrapper) `requires count > 0`, so a `count == 0` call
would violate that precondition.

- **Spec decision**: added `requires count > 0` to
  `PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_kernel_frames`, matching the contiguous
  allocator it delegates to. The sole caller (`mm::virt::manager::alloc_kpages`,
  not yet verified) must establish `count > 0`; this becomes an obligation when
  that module is verified.
- **Not auto-fixed**: adding a `count == 0` early return would change exec
  behavior of an unverified caller path. Recorded for the proving phase to
  decide whether to add the guard (code fix) or keep the precondition.

### OBS-2: `alloc_many_user_frames` distinctness depends on allocator non-aliasing

The Ok-arm contract now asserts `user_addr_set(frames@).len() == count` — the
`count` returned handles own *distinct* physical frames. This is the property
that closes the duplicate-frame / double-free hazard: without it, two handles in
`frames` could alias the same address, so `book_all` would reserve fewer than
`count` frames while the caller believes it owns `count`, and dropping both would
free the same frame twice.

  Ok arm of `alloc_many_user_frames`, and strengthened `lemma_user_bulk_ok`'s
  `ensures` with `user_addr_set(frames).len() == count` (body still `admit()`).
- **Proving-phase obligation**: distinctness must be discharged from the frame
  allocator's non-aliasing guarantee — each successful `frame::alloc` returns an
  address not currently in `free_frames`/`allocated_frames` overlap and removes
  it, so the per-iteration `push`ed addresses are pairwise distinct. This relies
  on `frame::alloc`'s (not-yet-verified) postcondition that the returned frame
  was free and becomes reserved. Recorded; no code change required.

### OBS-3: `alloc_kernel_frame` Err liveness vs. the `KernelFrame::new` failure path

**RESOLVED (spec phase, turn 2).** Turn 1's Fix D added an Err-arm clause
`old(self)@.free_count() == 0` (the liveness contrapositive: kernel allocation
fails only when no frame is free), discharged by an admitted lemma
`lemma_kernel_alloc_err_empty(pre) requires pre.wf() ensures
pre.free_count() == 0`. The reviewer (turn 2) correctly flagged this as
**unsound**: that lemma claims *every* well-formed partition has zero free
frames, which is `false`, and as a `pub proof fn` with `admit()` it was a
soundness landmine callable from any proof.

Root cause: `alloc_kernel_frame` has a **second** Err path —
`KernelFrame::new(frame_addr)` is fallible (`kframe.rs:84-100`:
`PageAligned::from_raw_value(...)?; crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(...)?`)
and runs *after* `frame::alloc()` already returned `Ok`. On that path a frame
*was* free (so `old(self)@.free_count() >= 1`), the frame is freed back (so
`final(self)@ == old(self)@` still holds), and the function returns `Err`. So
`old(self)@.free_count() == 0` is **false** on a real, reachable Err return.

**Resolution**: the wrap-failure outcome is **not observable** in
`FrameAllocView` — no field distinguishes "exhaustion" from "handle-wrap
failure" — so no abstract `free_count` clause can be soundly asserted on the Err
arm. The Err arm was corrected to the strongest sound statement, the
frame-condition alone:

```rust
Err(_) => final(self)@ == old(self)@,
```

The false `lemma_kernel_alloc_err_empty` proof fn and both its call sites were
**deleted** (`manager.proof.rs`, `manager.rs`). Whole-crate `admit` count
dropped 11→10 accordingly. `frame::alloc()?` was restored (no explicit `match`
needed once the Err-path lemma call is gone).

Evidence retained: `frame.rs:702-712` (`frame::alloc` Err spec = `true`),
`kframe.rs:74-100` (`KernelFrame::new` Err spec = `true`, fallible
`identity_map_page`). The `free_count()==0` liveness fact remains genuinely
inexpressible at this abstraction; if a caller ever needs it, the fix is an
exec-behavior change (make `KernelFrame::new` infallible in the kernel-frame
context, or convert wrap-failure to a panic) — out of scope for the spec phase.

33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
47.     }
48. }

51. // LinkedList — external type registration
52. //==================================================================================================
53. //
54. // `vstd` provides no specification for `alloc::collections::LinkedList`, so it must be
55. // registered as an external type before it can appear in spec signatures. Only the type
56. // is registered here; no `View`/iterator specification is provided, because the orphan
57. // rule forbids a downstream crate from implementing vstd's `View` / `ForLoopGhostIterator`
58. // traits for the foreign `LinkedList` / `linked_list::Iter` types. As a consequence, the
59. // two helpers that iterate a `LinkedList` in a `for` loop (`book_physical_memory_regions`,
60. // `book_mmio_regions`) cannot have their bodies verified and are `external_body`. See
61. // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`.

63. use ::core::alloc::Allocator;
64. 
65. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
66. #[verifier::external_body]
67. #[verifier::accept_recursive_types(T)]
68. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(A)]

71. //==================================================================================================
72. // Physical-memory subsystem view
73. //==================================================================================================
74. 
75. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by `mm::phys`.
76. ///
77. /// Pure ghost description — names no `MaybeUninit`, `AtomicBool`, bitmap, refcount slice,
78. /// or any other storage mechanism. It wraps the existing frame-allocator view
79. /// (`FrameAllocView`) with the two liveness facts the caller depends on.
80. pub ghost struct PhysModView {
81.     /// The frame allocator singleton has been initialized (`frame::init` ran
82.     /// successfully). All `frames`-related guarantees are meaningful only when this holds.
83.     pub initialized: bool,
84.     /// Abstract frame-allocator state: which physical frames are allocated (reserved) vs.
85.     /// free, with per-frame refcounts. This is the existing `FrameAllocView`.
86.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
87.     /// The `PhysMemoryManager` singleton has been initialized with a fresh user page pool.
88.     pub manager_ready: bool,
89. }
90. 
91. /// Current abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem.
92. ///
93. /// Uninterpreted accessor: the subsystem state lives in module-level singletons
94. /// (`frame::INSTANCE`/`INSTANCE_INIT` and the `PhysMemoryManager`/`Upool` singletons)
95. /// whose value is not directly spec-readable. The cross-call transition (`v -> v'`) is
96. /// realized in the proving phase by a ghost token over those singletons (see
97. /// `view_design.md` section 8); during the specification phase it is read like `self@`.
98. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysModView;
99. 
100. impl PhysModView {
101.     /// Well-formedness invariant of the subsystem.
102.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
103.         // Once the allocator is up, the frame partition is well formed.
104.         &&& self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
105.         // The manager layer can only be up if the allocator is up.
106.         &&& self.manager_ready ==> self.initialized
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// The subsystem is fully brought up and self-consistent.
110.     pub open spec fn live(self) -> bool {
111.         &&& self.initialized
112.         &&& self.manager_ready
113.         &&& self.frames.wf()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. //==================================================================================================
118. // Frame-set vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
119. //==================================================================================================
120. 
121. impl FrameAllocView {
122.     /// The allocator tracks (covers) the frame at `addr` — it is one of the frames this
123.     /// allocator knows about, allocated or free. Models `frame::is_covered`.
124.     pub open spec fn covers(self, addr: int) -> bool {
125.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) || self.free_frames.contains(addr)
126.     }
127. 
128.     /// The frame at `addr` is reserved: present in the allocated set, hence `alloc()` can
129.     /// never return it. This is the core caller-visible fact a "booked" frame satisfies.
130.     pub open spec fn reserved(self, addr: int) -> bool {
131.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr)
132.     }
133. 
134.     /// Every frame address in `set` is reserved.
135.     pub open spec fn all_reserved(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
136.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.reserved(a)
137.     }
138. 
139.     /// Every frame address in `set` is currently free (booking precondition: a range can be
140.     /// booked only if it is entirely free).
141.     pub open spec fn all_free(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
142.         forall|a: int| #[trigger] set.contains(a) ==> self.free_frames.contains(a)
143.     }
144. 
145.     /// Reserve every frame in `set` (each assumed free in `self`): move it from
146.     /// `free_frames` to `allocated_frames` with refcount 1.
147.     pub open spec fn book_all(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
148.         FrameAllocView {
149.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.union(set),
150.             free_frames: self.free_frames.difference(set),
151.             refcounts: self.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
152.                 Map::new(|a: int| set.contains(a), |a: int| 1int),
153.             ),
154.         }
155.     }
156. 
157.     /// Reserve only the *covered* frames of `set`; skip the rest (coverage-gated). Models
158.     /// the MMIO booking rule.
159.     pub open spec fn book_covered(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
160.         self.book_all(set.filter(|a: int| self.covers(a)))
161.     }
162. }
163. 
164. /// Page-aligned physical frame addresses covered by a region `[start, start + size)`.
165. /// Mirrors the frame-set computation used by `frame::alloc_range`.
166. pub open spec fn region_frame_addrs(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
167.     let start_frame_number = start / spec_page_size();
168.     let end_frame_number = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
169.     vstd::set_lib::set_int_range(start_frame_number, end_frame_number)
170.         .map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
171. }
172. 
173. /// The set of physical frame addresses covered by all regions in a physical
174. /// non-usable-memory list. Uninterpreted: `LinkedList` has no Verus model, so its contents
175. /// cannot be folded over in spec; this names the abstract union of `region_frame_addrs`
176. /// over the list, which is all the contract needs.
177. pub uninterp spec fn phys_regions_frame_set(
178.     regions: &::alloc::collections::LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
179. ) -> Set<int>;
180. 
181. /// The set of physical frame addresses covered by all MMIO regions in a list (after
182. /// GVA->GPA translation). Uninterpreted for the same reason as `phys_regions_frame_set`.
183. pub uninterp spec fn mmio_regions_frame_set(
184.     regions: &::alloc::collections::LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
185. ) -> Set<int>;
186. 
187. } // end verus!

---
name: bug-reporting
description: "Classify and report bugs found during Verus verification. Distinguishes true bugs from missing constraints and verifier limitations. Use when a verification failure might indicate a code bug."
---

# Bug Reporting

Finding real code bugs is a high-value outcome of formal verification.
Not every verification failure is a bug — ensure you have genuinely attempted
to prove it first (see `proving-guide`) before classifying a failure as one.

## Classification

After genuinely exhausting proof attempts (see `proving-guide`), classify
every remaining verification failure into one of three categories:

**True Bug** — the code is wrong regardless of calling context. No reasonable
precondition could make it correct (e.g. arithmetic overflow on all inputs,
logic error that always produces wrong results).

**Context-Dependent** — the code looks incorrect in isolation but may be
correct given constraints enforced elsewhere (e.g. callers guarantee bounds,
a system invariant ensures uniqueness). Check callers, upstream module specs,
and system-wide invariants before concluding it's a bug.

**False Positive** — the code is correct but verification fails due to
spec errors (overly strong postcondition, wrong invariant) or solver
limitations (trigger issues, quantifier reasoning gaps).

## When to Report

- **True Bug**: report immediately. This is the highest-value finding.
- **Context-Dependent**: report with analysis of what constraints would be
  needed and where they might come from.
- **False Positive**: do not report — fix the proof approach instead.
  Never weaken existing specs (requires/ensures) to work around a verification
  failure; see `verus-constraints`.

## Auto-Fixable Bugs

Some true bugs are mechanical and can be fixed immediately to unblock
verification. **Fix these directly in the source code** and commit with
the `[verus-ai] BUG FIX:` prefix so the fix is clearly attributed to
verification. Still record them in `bugs.md`.

Auto-fixable categories:
- **Arithmetic overflow/underflow**: missing checked arithmetic or bounds
  checks (e.g. `a + b` → `a.checked_add(b)`, or adding a bounds guard)
- **Off-by-one**: fencepost errors in loop bounds or index calculations
- **Missing bounds check**: index used without prior length/capacity check
- **Unchecked cast**: lossy `as` cast without range validation

For each auto-fix:
1. Make the **minimal** code change that fixes the bug
2. Record the fix in `bugs.md` with full details (see Report Format)
3. Add `// VERUS BUG FIX: <one-line description>` comment at the fix site
4. Re-run AST consistency — the fix is a **pre-approved deviation** (bug fix category)
5. Commit with `git commit --no-verify -m "[verus-ai] BUG FIX: <description>"` message
   (`--no-verify` is required because pre-commit hooks would reject exec changes)

No code bugs were found while proving `manager.rs`. Two source changes were
required and both are sanctioned by `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` (not bug
fixes):

- `PhysMemoryManager::init` and `kernel_watermark()` gained
  `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`. Verus cannot translate their bodies
  (`init` writes the `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER`; `kernel_watermark`
  reads the build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK` from a
  non-Verus crate). Both are already listed in `tcb-allowed.md`; without the
  attribute the crate does not compile under Verus.
- `check_user_watermark` was refactored to bind `let available =
  frame::free_count();` *before* the `kernel_watermark() + count` overflow
  check. This is behaviour-preserving (`free_count()` is a side-effect-free
  read) and lets the `available as nat == phys_view().frames.free_count()`
  postcondition supply the bound `free_count() <= usize::MAX` on every path,
  which the overflow `Err` arm relies on.

### Discharged (admit removed)

- **`lemma_free_count_bounded`** — deleted. The `<= usize::MAX` bound is now
  obtained soundly from `frame::free_count()`'s `usize`-typed result (see the
  `check_user_watermark` refactor above) instead of being assumed.
- **`lemma_kernel_bulk_err_restored`** — deleted (dead code, 0 call sites).
  The kernel contiguous-bulk `Err` arm proves `final(self)@ == old(self)@`
  directly from the loop invariant `self@ == g_old` (the kernel path never
  mutates `self@`: `frame::alloc_contiguous` is a free function).
- **`lemma_user_bulk_ok`** — deleted and replaced by a real inductive proof.
  `alloc_many_user_frames`'s loop now carries `user_bulk_inv`, discharged via
  proven helper lemmas (`lemma_user_addr_set_empty/_push`,
  `lemma_book_all_empty`, `lemma_book_all_alloc_one`, `lemma_user_bulk_base`,
  `lemma_user_bulk_step`). The `book_all`-accumulation and distinctness
  (`user_addr_set(frames@).len() == count`, OBS-2) follow from `Upool::alloc`'s
  real `&mut self` transition spec (`final@ == old@.alloc_one(uf@)`, `uf@`
  drawn from `old@.free_frames`), so each handle owns a distinct,
  previously-free frame.

### Remaining (irreducible within this module's scope — record only)

These 4 `admit()`s are the genuine §8 ghost-token / Drop trust boundary; they
are **not** dischargeable in `kernel::mm::phys::manager` without out-of-scope
changes, and forcing them would require unsound axioms:

- **`lemma_manager_attached`** (`m@ == phys_view().frames`). `m@ == m.upool@`
  (closed) and `phys_view()` are both `uninterp`; no axiom in scope links the
  manager/upool view to the global partition. The link is the §8 ghost-token
  attachment, realized by a token over the `frame::INSTANCE` singleton — which
  lives in the out-of-scope `frame` layer.
- **`lemma_kernel_alloc_one`** / **`lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous`**
  (`post == pre.alloc_one(addr)` / `pre.book_all(...)`). `frame::alloc` and
  `frame::alloc_contiguous` are *free functions* that do not take `self`, and
  `phys_view()` is a **constant** (parameter-free) accessor, so the pre→post
  partition transition is inexpressible at this layer (asserting it alongside
  `lemma_manager_attached` would even force `pre == post`). Expressing the
  transition needs a versioned/stepped ghost token threaded through the frame
  layer (out of scope; `frame.rs` and `phys_view()` are not modifiable here).
  Compare `Upool::alloc`, which *can* express its transition because it takes
  `&mut self` — that is exactly why the user bulk path was dischargeable above.
- **`lemma_user_bulk_err_restored`** (`m@ == pre` after `frames.clear()`).
  `clear()` drops the already-allocated `UserFrame`s, which frees them via
  `UserFrame::drop` → `frame::free`. Verus does not model `Drop` side effects
  on `self@`, so the restoration of the partition is genuinely unobservable in
  the exec model and must be asserted.

Net: manager `admit()` count 7 → 4. `make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys`
reports 0 errors (42 verified).

## Done — `make verify` passes with 0 errors

**Result:** Full `make verify` (all crates) exits 0 with **0 verification errors, 0 warnings**. Manager `admit()` count reduced **7 → 4**.

**Discharged (3 admits eliminated):**
- `lemma_free_count_bounded` — removed by binding `let available = frame::free_count()` before the overflow check (usize result gives the bound for free).
- `lemma_kernel_bulk_err_restored` — dead code (0 call sites), deleted.
- `lemma_user_bulk_ok` — replaced with a real inductive loop-invariant proof (new helpers: `user_bulk_inv`, `lemma_user_bulk_base/step`, `lemma_user_addr_set_empty/push`, `lemma_book_all_empty/alloc_one`). This path is provable because `Upool::alloc` exposes a `&mut self` transition spec.

**4 remaining admits — irreducible within module scope** (documented in `bugs.md`, classified record-only, NOT code bugs):
1. `lemma_manager_attached` — `m@` (closed `upool@`) vs `phys_view()` (constant `uninterp`); no in-scope axiom links them (§8 ghost-token attachment lives in the out-of-scope `frame` layer).
2. `lemma_kernel_alloc_one` / `lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous` — `frame::alloc*` are free functions and `phys_view()` is constant, so a pre→post transition is *inexpressible* (asserting one would force `pre==post`). Needs a versioned ghost token threaded through `frame.rs` (out of scope).
3. `lemma_user_bulk_err_restored` — relies on `frames.clear()` Drop side effects on `self@`, which Verus does not model.

No specs were weakened; only the two TCB-listed `external_body` additions (`init`, `kernel_watermark`) were used. Pushing the remaining 4 lower would require unsound axioms or out-of-scope edits to `frame.rs`/`phys_view()`, both prohibited by the task constraints.
